label: Loop over a list of items
description: Learn how a Loop repeats steps for every item in a list. The workflow gets 10 sample products from the free DummyJSON API, loops over them, logs each product under $20 and writes a summary when the loop is done. It runs with one click and needs no connection.

tasks.label: Get 10 products
tasks.name: httpClient_1
tasks.description: Gets 10 sample products, each with a title and a price, from the free DummyJSON API. The list is in ${httpClient_1.products}.

tasks.label: For each product
tasks.name: loop_1
tasks.description: Goes through the list in ${httpClient_1.products} one product at a time. The steps inside it see the current product as ${loop_1.item}.

iteratee.label: Is it under $20?
iteratee.name: condition_1
iteratee.description: Checks whether the price of the current product, ${loop_1.item.price}, is less than 20. Cheap products go to the True path; the rest are skipped.

caseTrue.label: Log the product
caseTrue.name: logger_1
caseTrue.description: Runs only for products under $20. Writes the title and price of the current item, ${loop_1.item.title} and ${loop_1.item.price}, to the log.

tasks.label: Log a summary
tasks.name: logger_2
tasks.description: Runs once, after the loop has finished. Writes how many products were checked, using ${httpClient_1.limit}.

stickyNotes.content:
## Start here: loop over a list

A **Loop** runs the steps inside it once for every item in a list. Inside the loop, `${loop_1.item}` is the item of the current round. This workflow goes through 10 sample products and logs the cheap ones. It needs no connection.

A ⚠ on steps that read the product data is normal: the editor cannot know the response fields before a run. The workflow still runs.

1. Click **Test** at the top to run it.
2. Click **Get 10 products** and open its **Output** tab: `products` is a list of items with a `title` and a `price`.
3. Click **For each product**. Its **List of items** field is `${httpClient_1.products}`, the list to go through.
4. Click **Is it under $20?**. It compares `${loop_1.item.price}` with `20`. Only cheap products reach **Log the product**.
5. Open **Logs** after the run: one line per cheap product, then the summary from **Log a summary**, which runs once, after the loop.
6. Change `20` to `100` and click **Test** again to see more products.
